 Federal prosecutors have filed criminal charges against two Illinois residents who allegedly defrauded the federal government of more than $29 million in a food stamp scheme that has ties to Greene County.
 Jorag Yaseen and Rami Kanaan operated retail food establishments in Chicago that processed thousands of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program transactions in 2024 and early 2025 that involved stolen account information from beneficiaries in Ohio and other states, say court records and a release from the U.S. Department of Justice. SNAP used to be called the food stamp program.
 The transactions were presented as legitimate food purchases, but no actual sales took place, and millions of taxpayer dollars were transferred to accounts controlled by the defendants and others, authorities said.
 Several wire transactions that occurred in March 2024 involved stolen SNAP electronic benefit card information that belonged to a Greene County resident, with losses totaling more than $1,200, court records and officials said. Yaseen and Kanaan allegedly used some of the money they received to buy cars for themselves and automobiles to ship overseas, officials said.
 The defendants were charged earlier this month in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Ohio with wire fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering.
 A local convenience store advertises that it accepts food stamps, which are now called Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits (SNAP).
 Cornelius Frolik / Staff
 Cornelius Frolik / Staff 
 Federal authorities in northern Ohio also recently charged three foreign nationals from Yemen and three others with SNAP benefits fraud, wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud.
 The defendants allegedly were involved in a criminal conspiracy to exchange Ohio SNAP benefit cards for cash, marijuana and other ineligible items as they worked at a gas station and convenience store in Euclid, which is located northeast of Cleveland. The defendants are accused of defrauding the food stamp assistance program of more than $1 million.
 “Every instance of SNAP fraud has two victims: families in dire need and taxpayers,” USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins said in a statement. “We are reminding fraudsters that we will find you and prosecute you to the fullest extent of the law.”
 ICE recently arrested several Haitian nationals who lived in Springfield and Ohio for allegedly receiving unlawful SNAP benefits. ICE has vowed to crack down on SNAP fraud involving immigrants who do not have authorization to live in the United States.
 In May, the U.S. Department of Agriculture released a report that says it identified $3 billion in annual SNAP spending that potentially could be fraud, waste and abuse. The USDA said the analysis was based on data from 29 state agencies that administer the SNAP program. The federal government spends about $101 billion on SNAP benefits annually.
 About 1.4 million Ohioans receive monthly food stamp benefits, and the state distributes about $237 million in benefits each month ($2.8 billion per year), according to state data.
 About 14,300 SNAP beneficiaries live in Greene County, which represents about 8.5% of the county’s total population. The average monthly distribution in Greene County is about $174.
 Elsewhere in the region, there are 77,130 food stamp recipients in Montgomery County (14% of the population); 38,460 recipients in Butler County (10%); 3,900 in Champaign County (10%); 21,500 in Clark County (16%); 9,700 in Miami County (9%); and 10,700 in Warren County (4%).
 Six years ago, a husband and wife and their Findlay Market vendor were sentenced in U.S. District Court in Dayton to food stamp fraud for exchanging cash for SNAP benefits.
 Busch’s Country Corner co-owner Michael Busch, his wife, Amanda Jo Busch, and his brother, Randall S. Busch, processed about $3.4 million in fraudulent SNAP transactions. Other criminal defendants several years ago were accused of fraudulently using electronic food stamp benefits at stores in Kettering and Troy.
